title: Cinsault
description: Also spelled Cinsaut, once called Hermitage in South Africa. A light, perfumed southern grape for rosé and fresh reds.
L: Cinsault gives pale to medium red wines with strawberry, raspberry, red cherry and floral notes, sometimes herbs. Tannins are low, acidity moderate. It's light, juicy and fragrant, often used to soften blends and in rosé. It's also a parent of Pinotage.

Cinsault, also spelled Cinsaut, probably comes from southern France, Languedoc or Provence. It tolerates heat and drought well, with large, juicy berries and thin skins. That gives high yields and pale colour, which is why it was used for bulk wine. From old, low-yielding vines, it gives perfumed, elegant reds.
Why does Cinsault often give pale wines?
Thin skins and a high juice ratio give pale colour and low tannin.

Look for pale ruby colour, bright red fruit and floral aromas, and a soft, light, juicy palate with little tannin. In blends, it brings perfume and softness. It's often compared with Pinot Noir or Gamay for its lightness, but it's warmer and more southern in feel.
Cinsault tolerates heat and drought well.
Yes. That's why it's common in the south of France, North Africa and South Africa.
Cinsault gives light, perfumed, soft red wine
It's heat-tolerant, with thin skins and big berries
Old vines give its most elegant wines

Cinsault grows across the Languedoc, Provence and the southern Rhône, mainly as a blending grape and in rosé. It was widely planted in Algeria and Morocco, and Lebanon's Bekaa Valley uses it, notably at Château Musar. South Africa and Chile's Itata Valley have old plantings.

In Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Côtes du Rhône, Cinsault adds perfume and softness to Grenache and Syrah. In the Languedoc, it softens Carignan. Its low tannin and freshness make blends more approachable. It's one of 13 grapes allowed in Châteauneuf.
Match each place to its Cinsault.
Cinsault spread around the Mediterranean and beyond.
Chile's Itata Valley has old, dry-farmed Cinsault vines planted long ago. Young producers there now make light, fresh, affordable reds from them.
What does Cinsault add to blends?
Cinsault grows across the south of France and beyond
Lebanon, South Africa and Chile have notable plantings

Cinsault's thin skins, low tannin and fresh red fruit make it ideal for rosé. It gives pale colour fast, with strawberry and floral notes. In Provence, it's a key partner to Grenache in pale, dry rosé. Tavel and Languedoc rosés use it too.

Cinsault, called Hermitage there in the past, was South Africa's most planted red grape until the 1970s, used for bulk wine and brandy. In 1925, Abraham Perold crossed it with Pinot Noir to create Pinotage. Today, young producers make fresh, light Cinsault from old bush vines, a revival of a forgotten grape.
Parent of Pinotage, revived from old vines
Which grape did Perold create by crossing Cinsault with Pinot Noir?

South Africa's Old Vine Project certifies vineyards over 35 years old, many of them Cinsault. Some, in Wellington and Darling, were planted in the early 20th century. Their low yields give concentration to a grape known for lightness. The wines are pale yet complex.
In South Africa, Cinsault was once called ____.
Hence the name Pinotage, from Pinot plus Hermitage.

Know how long to keep it

Cinsault's light body and soft tannin suit Mediterranean food: grilled fish, salads, charcuterie, roast chicken, mezze and tapas. Rosé suits seafood, salads and summer lunches. Its fruitiness handles mild spice, like Moroccan tagines or Lebanese dishes.
Serve red Cinsault slightly cool, 13 to 15 degrees, and rosé at 8 to 10. Most is best young, within two to three years. Old-vine wines and blends like Château Musar can age much longer.
What temperature suits a red Cinsault?
Slightly cool brings out its fruit and freshness.
Château Musar, from Lebanon, blends Cinsault with Cabernet Sauvignon and Carignan, and can age for decades. It's a rare chance to taste old Cinsault.
Most Cinsault is made for long ageing.
Not true. Most is best young, though some blends and old-vine wines age.
